title: B-Tree Index Internals: Leaf Pages, Splits, and Fillfactor
realWorldScenario: A high-frequency payment processing service experiences periodic latency spikes (from 4ms to 450ms) during bursts of INSERT statements into the `payments` table. Investigation shows high disk I/O on index files.
questionStatement: Explain how PostgreSQL B-Tree indexes handle insertions. What is an index page split, why does it trigger 50/50 page allocations and random I/O, and how does the `fillfactor` storage parameter alleviate this for high-update/insert workloads?
expectedConcepts: B-Tree 8KB leaf pages and (key, ctid) tuples
50/50 page split mechanics and write amplification
HOT (Heap-Only Tuple) updates and table fillfactor
Sequential vs random (UUID) index insertion patterns
hints: Think about what happens when an 8KB leaf page is 100% full and a new key falls between existing keys.
Contrast sequential integer IDs with random UUIDv4 keys.
Recall what HOT (Heap-Only Tuple) requires: the new row version must fit in the exact same 8KB table page.
